title: རྡོ་རྗེ་གཅོད་པའི་མདོ།
description: The Buddha dwells in the Jetavana forest near Śrāvastī with many monks, and the elder Subhūti rises to ask him a question about the path of the bodhisattva.

lineTranslations: Śrāvastī is a great city.
The Buddha dwells in Śrāvastī.
There is a forest in Śrāvastī. This forest is called Jetavana.
The Buddha dwells in the Jetavana forest.
The Buddha dwells in the Jetavana forest together with many monks.
Jetavana is Anāthapiṇḍada's forest.
Who is Anāthapiṇḍada?
Anāthapiṇḍada is a Buddhist.
The Buddha dwells in Anāthapiṇḍada's forest.
The Buddha enters Śrāvastī.
The Buddha enters Śrāvastī to eat.
The Buddha enters Śrāvastī to eat alms-food.
The Buddha wanders in Śrāvastī for alms.
The Buddha eats the alms-food.
Having eaten the alms-food, the Buddha returns to Jetavana.
Having returned to Jetavana, the Buddha sits down.

lineTranslations: The Buddha dwelt in Śrāvastī.
He dwelt in the forest called Jetavana together with many monks.
This forest is Anāthapiṇḍada's forest.
The Blessed One, having rested, took his bowl and robes and entered Śrāvastī.
He entered Śrāvastī to receive alms.
He wandered in Śrāvastī to get alms.
Having eaten his meal, he returned to Jetavana.
Having returned, he sat down.
He sat down after putting away his bowl and robes.

levels.textWylie:

lineTranslations: Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī.
He was dwelling in the Jetavana grove together with a great assembly of monks.
He was dwelling in that forest.
The Blessed One, having rested in the morning, taking his bowl and robes, entered the great city of Śrāvastī to eat alms-food.
Then the Blessed One wandered through the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
He, having sat cross-legged, having straightened his body upright, having established mindfulness, sat down.
Then many monks went to the place where the Blessed One was.
Those monks, having approached, having bowed their heads to the Blessed One's feet, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, sat down to one side.

phyin-nas bcom-ldan-'das-gi zhabs la mgos phyag-'tshal nas bcom-ldan-'das la lan-gsum bskor nas phyogs-gcig tu bzhugs-song.
lineTranslations: Homage to the Blessed Lady, the Perfection of Wisdom.
Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling in the Jetavana grove together with one thousand three hundred monks and many bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Then the Blessed One, having rested in the morning, taking his bowl and robes, entered the great city of Śrāvastī to receive alms.

Then the Blessed One, having wandered through the great city of Śrāvastī for alms, having eaten his food, having returned, having put away his bowl and robes, having washed his feet, having sat cross-legged on the prepared seat, having straightened his body upright, having established mindfulness, sat down.
Then many monks went to the place where the Blessed One was.
Having approached, having bowed their heads to the Blessed One's feet, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, they sat down to one side.

lineTranslations: Subhuti is a monk.
Subhuti is seated in the assembly.
Subhuti is seated in the assembly of monks.
Subhuti stands up.
Subhuti, having stood up, says this to the Buddha.
Amazing, amazing!
The bodhisattva mahasattvas are favored by the Tathagata with supreme favor.
The bodhisattva mahasattvas have been entrusted by the Tathagata with supreme entrustment.
A Buddhist might want to become a bodhisattva.
How should that Buddhist abide?

Excellent, Subhuti!

The bodhisattva mahasattvas have been entrusted by the Tathagata with supreme entrustment.
Listen, Subhuti!
I will speak for you.
I will speak for you how that Buddhist should abide.
May it be said by the Buddha.

The venerable Subhuti, having risen from his seat, having folded his hands in salutation to the Buddha, said this to the Buddha.
Buddha, it is amazing! It is amazing that the bodhisattva mahasattvas are favored by the Tathagata with supreme favor.
It is amazing that the bodhisattva mahasattvas have been entrusted by the Tathagata with supreme entrustment.
A Buddhist man or Buddhist woman might set out on the great vehicle.
How should that Buddhist abide? How should that one's mind be controlled?
The Buddha said this to the venerable Subhuti.
Excellent, Subhuti!
The bodhisattva mahasattvas are favored by the Tathagata with supreme favor.
The bodhisattva mahasattvas have been entrusted by the Tathagata with supreme entrustment.
Subhuti, listen. Attend well.
I will tell you how a Buddhist who has set out on the great vehicle should abide.
I will tell you how that one's mind should be controlled.

lineTranslations: At that time again, the venerable Subhuti was gathered in that very assembly.
He was seated.
Then the venerable Subhuti rose from his seat.
Having draped his robes over one shoulder, he placed his right knee on the ground.
Subhuti, having folded his hands in salutation, prostrated toward where the Blessed One was.
Having folded his hands in salutation, he said this to the Blessed One:
Blessed One, it is amazing! Well-Gone One, it is supremely amazing! It is so that the bodhisattva mahasattvas are favored by the Tathagata, the Arhat, the Fully Enlightened One, with supreme favor.
Blessed One, it is supremely amazing that the bodhisattva mahasattvas have been entrusted by the Tathagata, the Arhat, the Fully Enlightened One, with supreme entrustment.
Blessed One, a son of good family or a daughter of good family might set out on the great vehicle.
Blessed One, how then should that one abide?
How should that one practice?
How should that one's mind be controlled?
When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhuti:
Excellent, excellent, Subhuti.
It is so, Subhuti.
It is just as you have said.
The bodhisattva mahasattvas are favored by the Tathagata with supreme favor.
The bodhisattva mahasattvas have been entrusted by the Tathagata with supreme entrustment.
Subhuti, therefore listen.
Attend well and thoroughly.
I will tell you how a person who has set out on the great vehicle should abide.
I will tell you how that one should practice.
I will tell you how that one's mind should be controlled.
'Even so, Blessed One,' thus the venerable Subhuti said to the Blessed One.

བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས། ཡ་མཚན་ཏོ། བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་པ། མཆོག་ཏུ་ཡ་མཚན་ཏོ། དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་གིས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཆེན་པོ་རྣམས་མཆོག་ཏུ་རྗེས་སུ་བཟུང་བ་དང་མཆོག་ཏུ་གདམས་པ་ཡིན་ནོ།
བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས། རིགས་གི་བུ་འམ་རིགས་གི་བུ་མོ་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་ལ་ཞུགས་པ་དེ་ཇི་ལྟར་གནས་དགོས་སམ། ཇི་ལྟར་སྤྱོད་དགོས་སམ། དེའི་སེམས་ཇི་ལྟར་བསྡམ་དགོས་སམ།
དེ་སྐད་ཞེས་ཞུས་པ་ན་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་གིས་ཚེ་དང་ལྡན་པ་སུ་བྷུ་ཏི་ལ་འདི་སྐད་ཞེས་གསུངས་སོ།
ལེགས་སོ་ལེགས་སོ་སུ་བྷུ་ཏི། དེ་བཞིན་ནོ། ཁྱེད་གིས་ཞུས་པ་བཞིན་ནོ།
བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཆེན་པོ་རྣམས་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་མཆོག་ཏུ་རྗེས་སུ་བཟུང་བ་དང་མཆོག་ཏུ་གདམས་པར་གྱུར།
སུ་བྷུ་ཏི། དེ་བས་ཉོན། ལེགས་པར་དང་རབ་ཏུ་དྲན་པ་བཞག
བདག་གིས་ཁྱེད་ལ་བཤད་པར་བྱ་སྟེ་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་ལ་ཞུགས་པའི་གང་ཟག་དེ་ཇི་ལྟར་གནས་དགོས། ཇི་ལྟར་སྤྱོད་དགོས། དེའི་སེམས་ཇི་ལྟར་བསྡམ་དགོས།
བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་དེ་བཞིན་ནོ་ཞེས་ཚེ་དང་ལྡན་པ་སུ་བྷུ་ཏིས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ལ་ཞུས་སོ།

lineTranslations: At that time again, the venerable Subhuti, having gathered in that very assembly, was seated.

Then the venerable Subhuti, having risen from his seat, having draped his robes over one shoulder, having placed his right knee on the ground, having folded his hands in salutation toward where the Blessed One was, and having prostrated, said this to the Blessed One:

Blessed One, it is amazing! Well-Gone One, it is supremely amazing! It is so that the bodhisattva mahasattvas are favored and entrusted by the Tathagata, the Arhat, the Fully Enlightened One, supremely.
Blessed One, how should that son of good family or daughter of good family who has set out on the great vehicle abide? How should he practice? How should his mind be controlled?
When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhuti:
Excellent, excellent, Subhuti. It is so. It is just as you have said.
The bodhisattva mahasattvas are favored and have been entrusted by the Tathagata, supremely.
Subhuti, therefore listen. Attend well and thoroughly.
I will tell you how a person who has set out on the great vehicle should abide, how he should practice, and how his mind should be controlled.
'Even so, Blessed One,' thus the venerable Subhuti said to the Blessed One.
